messages:
Elaine: Quick check — we got a handful of client errors this morning where parsers blew up because the response had "text/plain" but the body was JSON. Also seeing confusion around optional nested fields (some services return null, others omit the key). Can we decide a stable behavior for /v1/infer responses so SDKs can be stricter?

Shiv: Short answer: we should standardize, long answer: tradeoffs. Do we force application/json and return 406 for anything else, or accept text/plain if it parses as JSON?

Mike: FYI the runtime usually sets Content-Type: application/json; some infra proxies are rewriting it to text/plain for streaming chunks. Breaking proxies is painful.

Ramona: For the nullable/absent keys piece: suggest documenting exact schema and using JSON Schema where optional fields that can be null explicitly use type: ["<type>", "null"]. Example: 
```
{
  "type": "object",
  "properties": {
    "result": { "type": ["object", "null"] },
    "metadata": { "type": ["object", "null"] },
    "error": { "type": ["string", "null"] }
  },
  "additionalProperties": false
}
```
That lets clients accept both null and present values. If you want to require presence, mark it in "required".

Shiv: +1 on explicit schema. For content-type negotiation: pragmatic approach: 1) always emit application/json from service, 2) accept text/plain in SDKs if body is valid JSON, 3) add a conservative warning header when we fallback (x-rw-content-coerced: 1) so we can detect proxies.

Mike: I can change the runtime to always set the header and include the coercion header when we have to coerce streaming chunks. Will add a small integration test.

Elaine: Good. For backward-compatibility policy let's: 1) keep accepting missing keys (don't break), 2) prefer returning null for explicitly-empty values for a single major version window, 3) publish schema and add contract tests. Also add a migration note in the SDK changelog.

Ramona: Also recommend adding a lightweight contract check in CI that validates a sample response against the canonical schema on every deploy. I can add the JSON Schema + a small python runner.

Shiv: Could we add a response header like x-api-schema-version so SDKs can opt into stricter validation? Then we can bump the schema version when we tighten the contract.

Mike: Implementing x-api-schema-version is trivial. We'll start with v1.0 and bump when we flip behavior.

Elaine: Cool — plan: Mike PR to set Content-Type consistently + x-rw-content-coerced, Ramona PR for schema + CI contract check, Shiv PR for SDK lenient parsing + watching header, and I'll draft the release note. I'll ping y'all for quick reviews. :thumbsup:

Shiv: noted, will watch the job. If anyone sees regressions in canary ping #eng-oncall.

Mike: Opening the runtime PR now, will tag ramona and shiv for review.

Elaine: Thanks — closing loop. If we need a follow-up sync I'll schedule a 15m.
